deckTitle: Dream-Wrestling with Kayfabe-Freud: Where the Id Always Kicks Out at Two!

cards.power:
The Basement Flood
Play this card to resurrect a discarded Quest Card from the beginning of the game.
cards.lore: It's not gone. It's just downstairs, lifting weights and waiting for you to fall asleep.
cards.gradeReason: Resurrection mechanic = pure theater. Players physically dig into discard. Lore hits.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: vintage horror comic. Subject: monstrous repressed faces in flooded basement. Mood: lurking, primordial.

cards.power:
Tip of the Tongue
The current player must finish their story without using the letter "I".
cards.lore: The waiting room of the mind. Ideas sit here until they are called or kicked out.
cards.gradeReason: Constraint forces immediate performance. Players will stumble out loud. Brilliant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir woodcut. Subject: men in trench coats in DMV waiting room. Mood: bureaucratic dread.

cards.power:
Redaction.
Interrupt a player. They must retell their last sentence using a euphemism.
cards.lore: He keeps at the door. He doesn't let the naked truth into the party.
cards.gradeReason: Live interruption + euphemism-on-demand. Table physics in three lines.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pulp comic. Subject: bald censor with TOP SECRET stamp, redacting nude figure. Mood: officious, leering.

cards.power:
Immediate Gratification
Take the die and set it to [6]. Describe your perfect victory.
cards.lore: Freud says: Every dream is a wish. Even the one where you lose your teeth.
cards.gradeReason: Player MUST monologue their fantasy. Performative win-state, pure invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: kids cereal box. Subject: ecstatic dog with golden bone trophy. Mood: triumphant, manic.

cards.power:
Zip File.
Combine two Scene cards into one stack. They are now a single entity.
cards.lore: Why have one anxiety when you can smash five faces into one monster? Efficient!
cards.gradeReason: Mechanic mirrors the concept perfectly. Players literally crush cards together.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surreal lithograph. Subject: cartoon faces crushed in giant trash compactor. Mood: comic absurdity.

cards.power:
Look Over There!
Move the Quest Die to a completely irrelevant Card on the Stage.
cards.lore: It's not about the Father. It's about the Father's coat button. Obsess over the button.
cards.gradeReason: Pivot mechanic + absurd lore tag. Pure misdirection theater.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: vintage horror comic. Subject: dragon ignored, child screams at coat button. Mood: misplaced terror.

cards.power:
Goo-Goo Ga-Ga.
Speak as your Actor, but with the vocabulary of a 3-year-old.
cards.lore: When the path forward is blocked, the mind runs backward to the crib.
cards.gradeReason: Forced regression-voice = instant table laughter. Knockout performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: charcoal sketch. Subject: adult man in diaper, crying in spotlight. Mood: pathetic, hilarious.

cards.power:
The Retcon.
Change the ending of the previous player's story to make it "make sense".
cards.lore: The lie we tell ourselves when we wake up, just to make the chaos look like a movie.
cards.gradeReason: Direct steal-and-rewrite mechanic. Tablecraft gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: silent film. Subject: top-hat showman painting over board game with patchwork. Mood: smug revision.

cards.power:
Boring Deja Vu.
You must incorporate a mundane object from the room you are currently in into the story.
cards.lore: The trash of yesterday becomes the treasure of tonight's hallucination.
cards.gradeReason: Breaks the fourth wall into the actual room. Forces immediate improv.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial ink. Subject: trash can with letters spilling out. Mood: mundane revelation.

cards.power:
Tantrum.
Flip the Quest Die over to its opposite side (1 becomes 6).
cards.lore: The oldest stuff lies deepest. You are still 4 years old and you want that cookie.
cards.gradeReason: Quick mechanical flip + invitation to throw a tiny tantrum. Two-second performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hidden-under-table. Subject: child kicking from beneath a chair. Mood: infant rage.

cards.power: Wake Up Call. Slam the table. All players must drop their hands.
cards.lore: The body is shouting, but the dream translates it into a symphony of pain.
cards.gradeReason: Literal table-slam mechanic. Whole room reacts. Maximum embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pulp horror. Subject: sleeper jolted by alarm and full bladder. Mood: rude awakening.

cards.power: Kayfa-BOOM! End the current Quest immediately. No winner.
cards.lore: The executioner of the dream. The return of the cruel, cold logic of 7:00 AM.
cards.gradeReason: Brutal game-ender. Drama-bomb in one play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gothic woodcut. Subject: screaming alarm clock face with teeth. Mood: tyrannical morning.

cards.power:
Cover Up.
Place this card over an Actor. They are now "The Gentleman".
cards.lore: According to Freud, if it fits on a head, it stands in for the... other head.
cards.gradeReason: Cute identity-swap. Joke is solid but mechanic could push performance harder.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: anatomy etching. Subject: top hat over phallic chess pawn. Mood: prim innuendo.

cards.power:
Rhythmic Motion.
Tap the table rhythmically while telling your story. If you stop, you lose your turn.
cards.lore: Up and down. In and out. The rhythm of the stairs is the rhythm of love. Allegedly.
cards.gradeReason: Physical rhythm constraint + dirty subtext. Embodied and funny.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: woodcut spiral. Subject: hypnotic staircase descending. Mood: trance, suggestion.

cards.power:
Symbolic Authority.
You are now the Boss. You decide who speaks next.
cards.lore: It hangs down. It is useless. Men wear it. Do the math.
cards.gradeReason: Conductor role is performative but mild. Lore tag carries the joke.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: limp realism. Subject: drooping tie alone on hanger. Mood: deflated authority.

cards.power:
Maternal Origin.
Treat this card as a "Home Base". Players can retreat there to avoid logic.
cards.lore: Mater comes from Mater (Mother). Wood is the universal mother-substitute. Don't ask.
cards.gradeReason: Safe-base mechanic is structural but quiet. Lore is the punchline.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark fairytale woodblock. Subject: tree shaped like mother silhouette. Mood: sheltering, eerie.

cards.power:
Castration Anxiety.
The next player loses one card from their hand (randomly selected).
cards.lore: Losing a tooth in a dream isn't about dentists. It's about losing your... power.
cards.gradeReason: Physical-loss mechanic + classic Freud beat. Tight invitation to grimace.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medical horror. Subject: pliers yanking molar from screaming mouth. Mood: visceral dread.

cards.power:
Erection.
Rise up from your chair. You must play standing up until your next turn.
cards.lore: Defying gravity. Rising up. The dream of flying is the dream of capability.
cards.gradeReason: Whole player physically rises. Maximum bodily commitment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: vintage sci-fi. Subject: steampunk rocket lifting off. Mood: phallic ascension, comic.

cards.power:
Surrender.
You may voluntarily discard your Actor to draw 2 new cards.
cards.lore: Falling is giving in. Sometimes you want to hit the bottom.
cards.gradeReason: Clean trade mechanic + invitation to dramatize collapse. Solid table beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: existential ink. Subject: tiny figure plummeting into void. Mood: surrender, release.

cards.power:
Unwanted Sibling.
Choose another player. They are now your "Rival". You must contradict them.
cards.lore: Small animals represent small children. Usually the ones you wish weren't born.
cards.gradeReason: Forced rivalry = instant table drama. Knockout interpersonal beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kafkaesque. Subject: cockroach in suit holding briefcase. Mood: unwanted, persistent.

cards.power:
Dad's Law:
Veto any story element that challenges authority.
cards.lore: The Father. The King. The Obstacle. He prohibits the fun.
cards.gradeReason: Veto power = strong table role. Players will weaponize it gleefully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: storybook monarchy. Subject: scowling king on throne crushing fun. Mood: paternal tyranny.

cards.power:
Mom's Favor:
Choose a player to protect. They cannot be challenged this round.
cards.lore: The Mother. The Object. The Origin. The Forbidden Zone.
cards.gradeReason: Protection mechanic creates alliance theater. Plus Oedipal punchline.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pre-Raphaelite. Subject: queen offering glowing apple. Mood: maternal seduction.

cards.power:
Sexual Tension.
Introduce a romantic subplot between two cards that really shouldn't be together.
cards.lore: Every dream about a burglar is a dream about a distinct kind of 'entry'.
cards.gradeReason: Forces players to romance two random cards on the spot. Maximum awkward gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir crime comic. Subject: cat burglar through window with sack. Mood: forbidden entry.

cards.power:
Projection.
Accuse another player of the strategy you are secretly using.
cards.lore: I'm not the bad guy. YOU are the bad guy who looks exactly like me.
cards.gradeReason: Pure psychological warfare encoded as mechanic. Will derail any game beautifully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: mirror-comic. Subject: two identical men pointing at each other. Mood: paranoid self-recognition.

cards.power:
Performance Anxiety.
Ask the active player a trivia question. If they fail, their turn ends.
cards.lore: You've already passed this test years ago. Why are you back here? To prove you're a fraud.
cards.gradeReason: Live quiz interrupt. Players will sweat. Tablecraft.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: anxiety dream sketch. Subject: naked student at unknown test. Mood: paralyzing exposure.

cards.power:
Exposure.
Reveal your entire hand of cards to the table.
cards.lore: It's not about skin. It's about the childhood wish to show off, gone wrong.
cards.gradeReason: Hand-reveal mechanic + classic dream beat. Brutal and direct.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Victorian woodcut. Subject: nude man calmly walking among crowd. Mood: dream-shame, public.

cards.power:
Stuck.
The Quest Die cannot be moved this turn, no matter the story.
cards.lore: You want to go, but your Will says 'No'. The conflict turns your legs to lead.
cards.gradeReason: Game freeze = embodied frustration. Mechanic IS the concept.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: expressionist ink. Subject: man trying to run, legs rooted. Mood: dream-stuck, futile.

cards.power:
Absurdity.
State a fact that is clearly false, but treat it as absolute truth.
cards.lore: If you dream they are dead, you secretly wished them dead. Don't look at me, Freud said it.
cards.gradeReason: Generic improv beat. Lore carries it but the mechanic isn't deck-defining.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gothic. Subject: grandmother knitting in rocking chair, slightly translucent. Mood: cozy uncanny.

cards.power:
Total Tragedy.
Destroy the current Stage. All scenes are discarded.
cards.lore: The ultimate plot twist: You were the detective AND the murderer all along.
cards.gradeReason: Nuke-the-table mechanic + iconic Freud beat. Maximum drama.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Greek tragedy comic. Subject: muscular figure gouging own eyes. Mood: cosmic horror.

cards.power:
The Riddle.
The active player must speak in a rhyme.
cards.lore: The gatekeeper of the story. Solve the riddle or get strangled by your own neurosis.
cards.gradeReason: Rhyme-constraint = instant table performance. Will produce gold and groans.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: classical engraving. Subject: sphinx with cigarette dangling. Mood: bored riddler.

cards.power:
Fate.
Force the story to take a tragic turn, regardless of logic.
cards.lore: Where you met the Father. Where you struck him down. Where it all went wrong.
cards.gradeReason: Solid story-pivot mechanic. Performative but slightly abstract.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dust-bowl noir. Subject: burning chariot at desert crossroads. Mood: doom convergence.

cards.power:
Hesitation.
Skip your turn to think about doing something, but do nothing.
cards.lore: He couldn't kill the King because he *was* the King in his dream. Analysis paralysis.
cards.gradeReason: Pass-turn via deliberate paralysis. Forces a beat of theatrical brooding.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink melodrama. Subject: jester holding skull, frozen mid-thought. Mood: paralyzed pondering.

cards.power:
Thick Plot.
Connect the current Story to at least 3 cards on the table.
cards.lore: Every dream image has ten different causes. It's a traffic jam of meaning.
cards.gradeReason: Forces synthesis. Works at table but is more cerebral than embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: alchemical chart. Subject: dense web of arrows between symbols. Mood: tangled meaning.

cards.power:
Show, Don't Tell.
You cannot use abstract words (love, freedom, justice). Only objects.
cards.lore: Dreams can't think 'Because'. They have to show two things crashing into each other.
cards.gradeReason: Vocabulary constraint = instant performance hack. Players will pantomime.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pulp art class. Subject: painter pointing at canvas labeled 'Constitutional Law'. Mood: literal absurdity.

cards.power:
Reverse Psychology.
Interpret the Quest Die's [1] as [6] and [6] as [1] for this turn.
cards.lore: In the unconscious, 'No' does not exist. Every 'No' is just a 'Yes' in a mask.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanical flip is solid but quiet. Lore does the heavy lifting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: protest poster. Subject: signs reading Left/No/Yes contradicting. Mood: contradiction.

cards.power:
Decoding.
Guess the hidden motive of another player. If right, take their card.
cards.lore: The dream is not a drawing. It is a puzzle text made of pictures. Read it, don't view it.
cards.gradeReason: Mind-reading bluff + card-steal stakes. Live psychoanalysis at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: rebus puzzle ink. Subject: eye + saw + sheep equation. Mood: cryptic decoding.

cards.power:
Free Association.
Say the first word that comes into your head. The next player must start their story with it.
cards.lore: Lie down. Don't look at me. Just talk until you say something shameful.
cards.gradeReason: Pure free-association engine. Forces immediate verbal spew. Classic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Vienna 1900. Subject: empty psychoanalyst's couch with rug. Mood: confessional invitation.

cards.power:
Block.
Cancel the effect of the last card played.
cards.lore: If you refuse to talk about it, that's exactly what we need to talk about.
cards.gradeReason: Counter-card mechanic + meta-Freud lore. Combat-clean.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: barricade woodcut. Subject: chairs piled against door. Mood: defiant blockage.

cards.power:
New Target.
Transfer the effect of a Power card to a different player.
cards.lore: You aren't mad at me. You're mad at your Dad. But I'm charging you by the hour, so go ahead.
cards.gradeReason: Redirect mechanic + cynical therapist lore = peak Freud satire.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: vintage therapy ad. Subject: patient yelling at calm analyst. Mood: misdirected fury.

cards.power:
Insight.
Look at the top 3 cards of the deck. Arrange them how you like.
cards.lore: The Royal Road to the Unconscious. Paved with bad intentions and dirty jokes.
cards.gradeReason: Top-deck manipulation = pure card-game power. Lore frames it as analyst sleuthing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Holmes pastiche. Subject: detective examining steaming poop with magnifier. Mood: comic analysis.

cards.power:
Primal Urge.
Ignore all rules for one turn. Just make something happen.
cards.lore: I want. I take. I eat. I kill. I sex. NOW.
cards.gradeReason: Rules-ignore mechanic = ultimate chaos card. Lore is a manifesto.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Heavy Metal magazine. Subject: yellow demonic face with neon teeth. Mood: primal hunger.

cards.power:
Compromise.
Move the Quest Die to the exact center [3.5] (or just say 3 or 4).
cards.lore: The poor clown trying to serve three masters at once. Reality, Id, and Super-Ego.
cards.gradeReason: Compromise mechanic mirrors the concept. The 3.5 joke is performative gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial caricature. Subject: man in suit juggling demons and angels. Mood: harried compromise.

cards.power:
Guilt Trip.
Another player apologizes for their story. They lose a turn.
cards.lore: The internalized parent. It watches you shower. It judges your thoughts.
cards.gradeReason: Forces a live apology from another player. Brutal social mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: stern engraving. Subject: looming Mosaic patriarch staring down. Mood: surveilling judgment.

cards.power:
Cathexis.
Add +1 to the Resonance [R] of any card on the table.
cards.lore: The fuel of the mind. It has to go somewhere. If you block it, it explodes.
cards.gradeReason: Quiet buff mechanic. Lore is great but mechanic is plumbing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: alchemical illustration. Subject: red liquid pouring through funnel into glowing vessel. Mood: charged transfer.

cards.power:
Memory Hole.
Remove a Scene card from the Stage. It never happened.
cards.lore: The best parts of the dream are the ones you can't remember. Trust me.
cards.gradeReason: Erase-from-existence mechanic. Players must pretend it never was. Tablecraft.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: open book ink. Subject: black hole burned into page. Mood: void, forgetting.

cards.power:
Unknowable.
This card cannot be removed or affected by any other card.
cards.lore: The spot where the dream reaches down into the unknown. Don't touch it.
cards.gradeReason: Solid immunity mechanic. Lore is mystical but mechanic is defensive plumbing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: anatomical etching. Subject: dark mushroom-navel descending into shadow. Mood: forbidden depth.

cards.power:
Fade Out.
Shuffle the discard pile back into the deck.
cards.lore: The sun comes up and the truth evaporates. Back to your safe, boring life.
cards.gradeReason: Reshuffle mechanic = useful but not performative. Lore is the meal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dawn watercolor. Subject: dreamscape dissolving into mist as sun rises. Mood: evaporating truth.

cards.power:
Capture.
Keep the last played Quest card as a Trophy.
cards.lore: Write it down fast, before the Censor wakes up and deletes the file.
cards.gradeReason: Trophy-capture mechanic. Functional, lore is the punchline.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bedside sketch. Subject: notepad with 'The Horse was a Toaster!!!' scrawl. Mood: feverish recall.

cards.power:
Mind Read.
Look at another player's hand.
cards.lore: Freud hated this stuff, but he couldn't quite rule it out. Spooky.
cards.gradeReason: Hand-peek = top-tier card-game power. Lore acknowledges Freud's secret embarrassment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: 1920s spiritualist. Subject: two brains in jars connected by lightning. Mood: occult science.

cards.power:
Repeat.
Play the same card you played last turn again.
cards.lore: I have been here before. Or maybe I just dreamed I was here. Whatever.
cards.gradeReason: Replay mechanic mirrors the concept. Simple, embodied, recursive.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: photocopy degradation. Subject: identical black cat photographed twice in alley. Mood: uncanny repeat.

cards.power:
Prediction.
Guess the number of the next die roll. If right, you win the Quest.
cards.lore: Is it the future? Or did you just wish for it so hard you made it happen?
cards.gradeReason: Live wager mechanic. Players will commit dramatically. Tablecraft.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: carnival mystic. Subject: crystal ball with explosion inside. Mood: foreboding prophecy.

cards.power:
Control.
Change the rules of the game for one round. (e.g., "High rolls lose").
cards.lore: I know I am dreaming. Therefore, I am God. Now watch this backflip.
cards.gradeReason: Rule-rewriting mechanic = god-tier card. Lore is the godhood manifesto.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: comic book hero. Subject: caped flyer in pajamas with hammer. Mood: drunk omnipotence.

cards.power: 1. Mix these with your Kayfabizarro Deck. 2. When you draw a Freud Card, things get weird. 3. Use "Freudian Logic" — if it makes no sense, it makes PERFECT sense. 4. Stay Fluffy.
cards.gradeReason: Instructional, but the 'Stay Fluffy' close = FrizzleBob signature. Onboarding done in 4 lines.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: storybook scroll. Subject: rabbit reading dusty leatherbound 'Die Traumdeutung'. Mood: scholarly mischief.

cards.power: If a player stumbles over a word, calls someone the wrong name, or giggles nervously: THEY MUST DRAW A CARD.
cards.lore: The Unconscious has spoken!
cards.gradeReason: Permanent table-watching rule. Turns every slip into a confession. Brilliant meta-card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: banana peel cartoon. Subject: tongue with bowler hat slipping. Mood: comic Freudian slip.

cards.power: Whenever a Long Object or a Hollow Object is mentioned, all players must nod knowingly and say "Aha!" If you fail to nod, lose a turn.
cards.gradeReason: Ongoing table ritual mechanic. Will derail every conversation. Perfect Freud joke.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: catalog illustration. Subject: cigar, train, key, padlock arranged neutrally. Mood: deadpan innuendo.

cards.power: Based on the delirious ramblings of S. Freud (1900). Distorted by Uncle FrizzleBob. No liability accepted for sudden realizations of incestuous desires. KayfaBIZARRO!
cards.gradeReason: Credits page. Performs as authorial signoff with proper disclaimer-comedy. Not a game card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tombstone woodcut. Subject: 'SIGGY 1900-Forever' headstone with dancing rabbit. Mood: irreverent eulogy.

verdict: FrizzleBob says: This deck is a tablecraft monster. The mechanics ARE the Freud concepts — Regression makes you speak baby talk, Resistance literally blocks a card, the Couch forces free-association out loud. Top strength: nearly every card is an immediate invitation to embody the concept, not explain it. Weakness: a few mid-deck cards (Crossroads, Overdetermination, Libido, Navel) drift toward abstract plumbing. The two NEW RULE cards on the back are evil genius — they keep playing after the deck is shuffled away. Table-ready Y.
blurb: Psychoanalytic wrestling expansion for the Kayfabizarro engine. 56 cards turn Freud's greatest hits — Id, Ego, Castration Anxiety, The Couch — into live performance constraints. For tables that want their improv with a side of repressed content.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — Vintage horror-comic poster with brain-wrestler vs. FrizzleBob-rabbit in a Mexican mask. Dense, layered, instantly readable as KK universe.
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'DREAM-WRESTLING with KAYFABE-FREUD' + subtitle 'Where the Id always kicks out at two!' — the title IS the pitch.
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Hits the Kayfabizarro main-line tone perfectly: pulp, German, satirical, brainy.
coverQA.coverOriginality: 4 — Strong concept-marriage (Freud + lucha). The brain-luchador image is fresh and ownable.
coverQA.coverViral: 5 — 'Contains 100% Repressed Content' + 'Do not eat the cards.' are screenshot-ready taglines.
coverQA.coverNote: FrizzleBob says: Cover is doing the work of a billboard, a manifesto, AND a comic-shop window. Every micro-element earns its space — the date stamp, the warnings, the BLÖDSINN! caption, the skeleton in pink. Could lose half the speech bubbles without harm, but the over-stuffing IS the vibe.

notes: 15-page deck = cover (page 1) + 52 numbered cards across pages 2-14 (4 per page, 2x2 grid) + 4 panels on page 15 (HOW TO USE + 2 NEW RULE meta-cards + CREDITS & BLAME) = 56 cards total. RAF dice boxes (R red / A yellow / F blue colored cubes) present on every card in stat-bar row. Bilingual German subtitles on most card names (Das Unbewusste, Die Zensur, Der Wunsch...) reinforce the Vienna-1900 Freud register. Footer marginalia is dense (BLÖDSINN!, HUMBUG!, Aha!, KayfaBINGO!, KAYFABOGGLE!, Stay fluffy!, Daddy Issues?, FREUD WAS RIGHT!, MOMMY DEAREST, etc.) — these are not card content but vibe-armor. Card 40 (Interpretation / Detective) has a dual title bar — appears to be one card with two names. The 'Contains 100% Repressed Content' banner and 'Do not eat the cards' warning on cover should be preserved in any reprint. Date stamp on cover: OCT 26, 1978 — APR (continuing). Tagline on cover: MADNESS ARENA. This file overwrites an earlier 2026-05-03 claude_sonnet_4_6 analysis to apply the v3 schema and re-verify all power/lore text against the actual PDF pages.

quickWins: Clarify card 40 — confirm whether INTERPRETATION and DETECTIVE are the same card or a printing artifact
Promote NEW RULE cards visually so buyers don't miss them at end of deck
niceToHave: Add a one-page Freud-glossary insert for non-German players
Cross-reference card with Psycho_Karaoke_Kult and Carnival_of_Unsolved_Problems THERAPY deck in bundle copy

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: DREAM-WRESTLING WITH KAYFABE-FREUD – Where the Id Always Kicks Out at Two (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Freud built a fight club in 1900 and had the nerve to call it a clinic.

A century of wellness merchants have sanded him down into a soothing rerun: name the trauma, process the feeling, tie a bow on it, feel resolved by Tuesday. That is the real repression. The drives Freud described do not get cured and they do not get closure. They get held down for a three-count, kick out at two, and come back wearing a different mask. Any therapy that promises you a clean ending is selling the same tidy lie that put you on the couch in the first place.

This is the couch as a wrestling mat: 56 cut-and-play cards that turn the Id, the censor, and the slow burn of transference into live performance constraints. Social Story Wrestling for the unconscious, you perform the drives out loud, you commit to whatever surfaces, and the table decides what gets repressed and what breaks the pin. Built for improv tables that want their scenes with a side of unmistakably repressed content.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Kayfabe-Freud Core Deck: 56 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring THE COUCH (Die Couch), where the patient lies down and the whole match changes hands, TRANSFERENCE (Übertragung), the move that makes you fight your analyst as if they were your father, and THE ID (Es), the one opponent that never tires and never agrees to stay down.
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the RAF dice in every stat bar deciding whether your Repression, Acting-out, or Free-association carries the round.
- The Madness Arena Engine: a Vienna-1900 register where German subtitles ride every card name, the Wunsch wrestles the Zensur for control of the dream, and "100% Repressed Content" is a promise the deck keeps every single hand.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
This deck is part of the Kayfabizarro main line. Grab it and you are not buying a frozen PDF, you are on the Protopian Pipeline: every future expansion, drive, and dream-act in this cycle reaches you as a free update, no second checkout.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I trust a story that fights back more than a feeling that has been processed into silence, so I made the analysis a contact sport. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Play it. Stage it on whatever couch you have. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the next batch of cards.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"You never pin the Id. You just learn to wrestle it where people can watch."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
